question.problem:
Given the **orthonormal** basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $\sqrt{6}{x}_{2}$, where ${x}_{2}$ is the second component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{30}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{30}} \\ -\frac{5}{\sqrt{30}}\end{aligned}]\},\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ -8\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2},\,{q}_{3}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=x\cdot {q}_{i}.$ Computing ${x}_{2},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =x\cdot {q}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ -8\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{6}}+\frac{10}{\sqrt{6}}-\frac{8}{\sqrt{6}} \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{6}} \\  & =\sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\sqrt{6}{x}_{2}=\sqrt{6}\cdot \sqrt{6}=6.
$$
